text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Branko Crvenkovski in an interview predicted two percent inflation for 1997. He said the denar would remain stable and the gross domestic product would increase to five percent. He denied speculation of a shake-up of his government and declared victory for his Social Democratic Party in November's local elections.
- President Kiro Gligorov welcomed 1997 in his New Year message, saying "the democratic process in Macedonia, economic reforms and reintegration into European associations and NATO should continue".

- Minister for Culture Slobodan Unkovski said he risks being called "the minister for ruining Macedonian cultural institutions". He said the system for financing cultural activities must be changed. "The institutions and traditional manifestations can not be financed from the ministry any more," he said.

- Macedonia's most significant event was the split of the Alliance for Macedonia (Social Democratic Party, Liberal Party and Socialist Party) last February when the Liberal party joined the opposition, comments Dnevnik.
